Platform and Enclosure Build

Magnetic door revision · Adapted from the original Claude artifact. Original assembly illustrations show the enclosure before the magnet pockets were added.

How to build the four-cell platform from a 10 in base sheet and a 12 in top plate, and fit it into the birdhouse enclosure with its drains and D5-1A solar kit. It covers every measurement, part and piece of hardware, in the order you assemble them.

Measure the base sheet before sending the tray to the BigRep. The inset is sized for exactly 10 × 10 × 1/4 in. Cut plastic sheet is often slightly off, and the inset only allows 0.75 mm each side. Measure yours with calipers. If it falls outside the tray fit, obtain the matching enclosure source before changing the inset. The checked-in platform generator covers the plywood version.

Two more sizes are still estimates. The box assumes a bucket with a 15 in top rim and a 17 in height, handle folded (BUCKET_TOP_D, BUCKET_H). The D5-1A's size and bracket hole spacing aren't confirmed either, so its pictures are sketches. The mounting pad doesn't depend on the hole spacing, but check that the antenna clears the eave.

Assembly

0 of 16 done
  1. Prepare the prints
  2. 1

    Clean up the prints

    • Drill every hole in the table above to size.
    • Trim strings out of the gasket channel on the door back and off the rib on the door frame. The rib has to sit cleanly in the channel.
    • Clean up the inset in the tray, and test-fit the base sheet. It should drop in without forcing. If it binds, sand the inside of the inset wall rather than the sheet.
    • Push the hinge rod through the three body knuckles, then the two door knuckles, to check each set lines up before you hang the door.
  3. 2

    Seal the outside

    Needs: body, door, handle, port hood, exterior paint or bedliner

    • Large-nozzle prints have small gaps between layers. Sand off loose strings, wipe the parts clean, and paint every outside face.
    • Give the roof a second coat, including the underside of the overhangs; water runs across the most layer seams there.
    • Keep paint out of the gasket channel, off the frame rib and out of the hinge knuckles. Let it cure fully before the next step.
  4. 3

    Fit the feet to the body

    Needs: body, 4 riser feet, 4 bolts, 8 nuts, 4 fender washers

    • Drop a bolt head into each foot's hex pocket with a dab of silicone so the foot stays on when you lift the box.
    • Run a nut up each bolt about 20 mm, then push the bolt up through a floor corner hole.
    • Inside, add a fender washer and the second nut. Leave them finger-tight; you level the box in the last step.
  5. Build the platform
  6. 4

    Drill the base sheet and bolt on the adapters

    Needs: 10 × 10 × 1/4 in sheet, 4 holder adapters, 12 #6-32 × 5/8 in flat-head screws and nuts

    • Print four-cell/template-base.pdf at 100% / Actual size. It's one page. Measure the 2 in square both ways.
    • Cut along the two thick lines. Put the cut corner on a corner of the sheet, edges flush, and tape it down.
    • Punch through all 3 crosses with a centre punch or a nail. Move the template to the next corner and repeat, until you have 12 marks.
    • Clamp the sheet to scrap wood and drill every mark with a 5/32 in bit, so the plastic doesn't tear out on the far side.
    • Bolt on the four holder adapters from the top, 3 screws each, with every adapter's notch pointing at the centre of the sheet. Tighten the nuts underneath until snug; overtightening dimples a sheet this thin.

    Printed platform: the adapters are already part of the base, so skip this step. Don't use wood screws on the sheet: they'd come out the other side.

  7. 5

    Seat the load cells

    Needs: 4 load cells, 4 V3 holder bases and caps, 24 AWG wire

    • Put each cell in a V3 base and set the base in an adapter, with its wire slot in the adapter's notch.
    • Extend each cell's leads so they reach the back wall. The farthest cell needs about 650 mm in total.
    • Run the wires flat along the sheet to its back edge and tape them down.
    • Snap a cap onto each holder.
  8. 6

    Fit the bucket tabs and locator rings

    Needs: 12 × 12 × 1 in plate, 4 locator rings, 4 bucket tabs, 20 pan-head #6 screws, foam tape

    • Bucket tabs: use four-cell/template-top.pdf the same way, on the plate's top face: 2 crosses per corner, 8 marks. Drill them 7/64 in, 12 mm deep (wrap tape round the bit at 12 mm), and screw on the four tabs.
    • Locator rings need no template. Drop a ring over each cap boss on the base sheet, and stick a piece of foam tape on top of each ring.
    • Lower the plate onto the bosses, tabs up, with 1 in of overhang on all four sides. Press down over each ring. Write FRONT on the same edge of the plate and the base sheet.
    • Lift the plate. The rings come with it, each exactly where its boss is. Turn it over and drill through each ring's 3 holes, 7/64 in, 12 mm deep.
    • Take each ring off, peel off all the tape, and screw it back on with 3 screws. Left on, the tape would drop the ring onto the cap and take weight off the cell.
    • Set the plate aside. It goes on in step 9.

    Printed platform: the rings are printed in. Only screw on the bucket tabs (8 screws).

  9. Put it in the enclosure
  10. 7

    Fit the drains and the tray

    Needs: body, tray, silicone, stainless mesh scrap

    • Inside the body, glue a scrap of mesh over each of the two floor drain holes.
    • Run a ring of silicone on the floor round each drain hole, so water can't get under the tray.
    • Lift the tray over the 30 mm sill and lay it on the floor. The corner notches go over the foot nuts, and the tray's two 16 mm drains (blue in the top picture) land over the floor holes.
    • Pour a cup of water at the back of the tray. It should all run out through the two drains. If it pools, check the box is level, then fix that before going on.
  11. 8

    Drop the base sheet into the inset

    Needs: base sheet with its holders and cells

    • Lower the sheet into the inset with its FRONT edge toward the door. It rests on the ribs, and the nuts drop into the pockets cut in the ribs.
    • Check it can't slide: the inset wall holds it about 0.75 mm clear on every side. If it rocks, a nut is touching. Back it off or trim the screw end.
  12. 9

    Mount the HX711 and set the top plate on

    Needs: HX711, HX711 tray, 4 pan-head #6 screws, PG7 gland, lever connectors, gel pack, top plate

    • Fit the PG7 gland in the HX711 tray. Coat the HX711 board with conformal coating, let it dry, and put it in the tray with the gel pack.
    • Run the cell wires from the back edge of the sheet, low across the tray and up the back wall, in through the groove in the pad. Wire the bridge as in four-cell/wiring-load-cells.png.
    • Screw the tray to the pad on the back wall with its open face against the pad, 4 screws.
    • Lower the top plate onto the four cap bosses so each ring drops round a boss, FRONT mark toward the door.
    • Slide paper all the way round between the plate and everything below it. No wire or part may touch the plate.
  13. Finish the enclosure
  14. 10

    Fit the door gasket

    Needs: door, 2 m of foam weatherstrip

    • Wipe the channel between the two ridges on the door back with isopropyl alcohol.
    • Start at the middle of the bottom edge. Peel the backing as you go and press the foam into the channel without stretching it; ease it round the 20 mm corners.
    • Butt the two ends together tightly at the start.
  15. 11

    Fit the handle

    Needs: door, handle, 6 #10 × 1 in pan-head screws

    • Hold the handle on the door front along the right (non-hinge) edge, so its three ears stick out past the edge with their holes outside the door.
    • Drive the 6 screws from the back of the door through the clearance holes into the ears.
  16. 12

    Hang the door

    Needs: hinge rod, 2 M6 nuts and washers

    • Hold the door's two knuckles between the body's three on the left side.
    • Slide the rod through all five from under the roof overhang. Put a washer and nut on each end.
    • Swing the door: it should open past 90° without rubbing. Shut it and check the frame rib lands in the gasket all the way round.
  17. 13

    Install the magnetic catches

    Needs: four Ø20 × 3 mm discs, outdoor two-part epoxy, masking tape and a straightedge

    • Dry-fit all four magnets. Each printed pocket is Ø21.5 mm × 3.5 mm deep. Deburr by hand as needed and keep paint out of the pockets and off the magnet faces.
    • Snap the magnets together in pairs. Separate one pair at a time and mark the two faces that were touching. Install the marked faces outward, so each body magnet attracts its door partner. Keep the pairs labeled until bonded.
    • Clean the pocket and magnet backs. With the part face up, set each disc in epoxy. Use thin nonmagnetic shims as needed to position its face just below the surrounding plastic (about 0.1 mm). Use a straightedge to check. Seal around the disc edges with epoxy and wipe the faces clean.
    • Let the epoxy fully cure before bringing the pairs together. Close the door slowly and check that the magnets pull it shut, the gasket contacts around the rim, and the door opens freely by the handle. The nominal magnet face gap is about 0.8 mm with this setup. Printed dimensions and gasket stiffness affect the result.
    • Check that the door stays closed with the pins withdrawn. Use the original pins for positive closure in wind, during transport, or if the magnets alone leave a gap at the gasket.
  18. 14

    Fit the cable gland and port hood

    Needs: PG7 gland, HX711 cable, 16 mm grommet, port hood, 2 M4 × 12 bolts and nuts

    • Fit the PG7 gland in the hole just under the HX711 pad (right of centre, seen from the front). Run the HX711 cable out through it, long enough to reach the side you'll mount the solar kit on, and tighten the gland.
    • Fit the grommet in the high hole in the back wall. Bolt the port hood over it with the two M4 bolts, open side down.
    • Feed the sap drop line up into the hood from below and through the grommet into the bucket. Let the line sag into a drip loop below the hood so water running down it drops off first.
  19. 15

    Mount the D5-1A solar kit

    Needs: D5-1A kit and its bracket, 1/8 in drill bit

    • Each side wall has a solid 120 × 120 mm pad near the back. Choose the side that will face south. The other pad stays spare.
    • Hold the bracket on the pad, mark through its holes and drill 1/8 in pilots no deeper than 25 mm.
    • Drive the bracket's screws. They must be 1-1/8 in (29 mm) or shorter: pad plus wall is 30 mm, and a longer screw would come through into the box. Use shorter #8 wood screws if the kit's are too long.
    • Fit the panel on the bracket and tilt it toward the sun. Check the antenna stands clear of the eave, which sticks out 60 mm from the wall.
    • Connect the HX711 cable to the ESP32 through the D5's cable entry, with a drip loop below the entry.
  20. 16

    Place, level and stake it

    Needs: 3 tent stakes, 2 hitch pins, a level, the bucket

    • Pick a spot that doesn't collect meltwater, or stand the feet on pavers. Turn the box so the solar kit faces south and the panel has open sky.
    • Level it on the top plate using the feet: turn the lower nut on each bolt to set its height, then lock with the nut inside. The floor ends up 60 to 90 mm off the ground.
    • Drive stakes through the two rear corner lugs.
    • Stand the bucket on the top plate between the four tabs. Shut the door.
    • Drive the front stake through the handle’s bottom ear and the body lug to anchor the front. Withdraw it from the ear before opening the door.
    • The magnets hold the door for routine access. Use the middle and top hitch pins when you need positive closure or extra gasket compression.

Check the readings

  1. Fill the bucket a gallon at a time (8.34 lb each). The readings should rise in equal steps.
  2. With the bucket full, push on the side of the box and on the door. The reading must not change; if it does, something is touching the top plate.
  3. Leave the bucket full overnight. A reading that drifts means something is creeping or rubbing; look first at the V3 cap skirts (see the README).

Keeping it dry through the season

  • The roof sheds snow and rain to the sides, but the enclosure isn't watertight. Inside, condensation is a bigger risk to the electronics than snow getting in.
  • When you check the bucket, check the silica gel pack. Swap it when it changes colour, and dry the old one out indoors.
  • Check that the two floor drains aren't blocked, from under the box. A blocked drain leaves water sitting under the base sheet.
  • Clear snow banked against the box. Meltwater from a drift can come back in through the drains.
  • If the door freezes shut, warm the gasket edge with your hands; don't pry the door, because PETG gets brittle in deep cold.
  • Touch up the paint each autumn before it goes back out.

This revision uses the supplied enclosure STLs. The magnet geometry is included in the linked body and door meshes. Use the supplied base drilling template and top drilling template for the sheet platform.
